places.name: Digne
places.today: Digne-les-Bains, prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence.

tagline.text: Small cathedral town in the mountains of Provence, seat of Bishop Myriel’s poor, roadless diocese.
Mountain town where every door is shut on a released convict except the Bishop’s.

places.name: The Bishop’s house
places.today: Hugo’s model was Bishop Miollis, Bishop of Digne from 1805 to 1838.

tagline.text: The cramped old hospital the Bishop takes in exchange for his palace; its door is never locked.
The Bishop’s little house, where a convict is given the alcove bed and the silver candlesticks are lit.
The Bishop’s little house, where the gendarmes bring back the silver and the Bishop gives away his candlesticks too.
Digne’s best inn, whose landlord Jacquin Labarre turns the traveller away.
The hidden valley near Digne where the old member of the Convention lives alone and dies.

places.name: Aix
places.today: Aix-en-Provence.

tagline.text: Old Provençal capital, where Myriel’s father was a magistrate.

places.name: Brignolles
places.today: Brignoles, Var.

tagline.text: Provençal town where Myriel was curé before he became a bishop.
Mountain village and old bishopric of the diocese; the Bishop rides in on an ass.
Alpine town with an old cathedral, Notre-Dame d’Embrun.
Alpine town whose cathedral sacristy the brigand Cravatte robbed.
High Alpine town the Bishop holds up as an example: there widows and orphans mow first.
High Alpine town near which the escaped convict left traces of his flight.
Alpine valley town; Cravatte’s band hides in the mountains above it.
Hill town above the Riviera and old seat of a bishop.
Perfume town where Valjean, a day out of the galleys, is paid half wages and warned of the prison.

places.name: The galleys of Toulon
places.today: The bagne of Toulon, inside the naval arsenal, closed in 1873.

tagline.text: Naval port of Provence and its galleys, where Jean Valjean served nineteen years.
The galleys where Valjean became No. 24,601 and tried four times to escape.
The galleys, to which Valjean is sent back for life as No. 9,430.
The naval port, where the damaged Orion puts in for repairs and a convict falls from the rigging.
Town in the Jura, near the Swiss border, where the convict says he is bound; famed for its cheese-dairies.

places.name: Faverolles
places.today: Hugo places it in Brie; the Faverolles he had in mind is usually taken to be this village near Villers-Cotterêts, in the Aisne.

tagline.text: Village where Valjean was a tree-pruner and stole a loaf for his sister’s children.

places.name: Bicêtre
places.today: Now the Bicêtre hospital, Le Kremlin-Bicêtre.

tagline.text: Prison south of Paris where the chain-gangs were riveted before the march to the galleys.
Headland east of Toulon harbour where the swimmer came ashore by night.
Shore across Toulon roads, where a country house outfitted escaped convicts with clothes.
Village north-west of Toulon, the first stage of the escaped convict’s flight.

places.name: Accons
places.today: Probably Accous, in the Aspe valley.

tagline.text: Pyrenean village where traces of the fugitive were later found.
Town in the Périgord, a last trace of the fugitive before Paris.
Southern city, Tholomyès’s home.
Southern city, where the Toulouse diligence carries the four students home.

places.name: Fontevrault
places.today: Fontevraud Abbey.

tagline.text: Great royal abbey on the Loire, the centenarian nun’s first convent.
The capital, where Myriel caught Napoleon’s eye.
Restoration Paris in 1817, the city of the four students and their grisettes.
Paris, where a white-haired stranger in a yellow coat looks for lodgings on its southern edge.
Park and palace west of Paris, where the four couples spend their summer Sunday.

places.name: Issy
places.today: Issy-les-Moulineaux.

tagline.text: Village south-west of Paris, with Bourguin’s park and its swing.
Restaurant in the Champs-Élysées, looking over the quay and the river, where the picnic ends at dinner.
Restaurant in the Champs-Élysées where the four girls wait for their ‘surprise’.
The botanical garden and menagerie on the Left Bank.
The botanical garden on the Left Bank, skirted by its lower streets on the way to the river.
Bleak boulevard on the southern edge of Paris, by the Salpêtrière.
Bleak, deserted boulevard by the Salpêtrière, where the man in the yellow coat hires a room.

places.name: The Gorbeau house
places.today: Demolished; the house and its exact site are Hugo’s, on a boulevard that still exists.

tagline.text: Ramshackle tenement, No. 50–52 Boulevard de l’Hôpital, at the corner of the Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel.
Ramshackle tenement on the Boulevard de l’Hôpital, where Jean Valjean and Cosette take the attic.
Ramshackle tenement on the Boulevard de l’Hôpital, which Valjean and Cosette flee by night.
Parish church near the Gorbeau house, where Valjean gives alms at nightfall.

places.name: The Rue des Postes
places.today: Renamed the Rue Lhomond.

tagline.text: Old street of the Mouffetard quarter where Valjean, hidden in a doorway, watches four men confer.

places.name: The Pont d’Austerlitz
places.today: Rebuilt in stone in 1854 on the same site; it links the Gare d’Austerlitz to the Bastille side.

tagline.text: Bridge over the Seine below the Jardin des Plantes.
Toll bridge over the Seine below the Jardin des Plantes; two sous for a man carrying a child.

places.name: The Rue du Chemin-Vert-Saint-Antoine
places.today: Hugo’s street; the quarter between the bridge and the Faubourg Saint-Antoine was rebuilt from top to bottom.

tagline.text: Little street between two walled timber-yards, opening off the right bank above the bridge.
Little street off the right bank, where a deaf fruit-seller minds Cosette for a day.

places.name: The convent of the Petit-Picpus
places.today: The convent, the Rue Polonceau and the Rue Droit-Mur are Hugo’s invention, set on ground later covered by the Mazas prison, the Boulevard Diderot and the Gare de Lyon.

tagline.text: Half-forgotten quarter of walls, gardens and convents between the Faubourg Saint-Antoine and La Râpée.
Walled convent garden in the Petit-Picpus, where old Fauchelevent is gardener.
No. 62 Rue Petit-Picpus, convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration.
No. 62 Rue Petit-Picpus, the Bernardine convent where Cosette becomes a pupil and Valjean a second gardener.

places.name: The Vaugirard cemetery
places.today: Closed in 1824, when the Montparnasse cemetery replaced it; built over.

tagline.text: Old cemetery outside the Vaugirard barrier, where the convent’s nuns have a corner of their own.
Faded old cemetery off the Boulevard du Maine, which shuts at sundown; next door is the dram-shop Au Bon Coing.

places.name: The Barrier of Monceaux
places.today: Its rotunda survives at the entrance to the Parc Monceau.

tagline.text: Toll gate in the city wall on the north-west side of Paris.
Open ground before the Paris Observatory, where the cabriolet sets down a man and a child.
Village east of Paris, where Fantine leaves the coach to walk to Montfermeil.
Village on the wooded plateau east of Paris, on the road to nowhere.
Forest village short of water, whose only spring by the church end lies a quarter of an hour away.
Thénardier’s cook-shop at Montfermeil, where Fantine leaves Cosette.
The Thénardiers’ failing inn, where Cosette drudges and the village calls her the Lark.
The Thénardiers’ inn, where a stranger in a yellow coat pays fifteen hundred francs to take Cosette away.
The little spring halfway down the slope toward Chelles, where Cosette must fetch water after dark.
The forest spring where Cosette fills her bucket alone on Christmas Eve.
The woods round Montfermeil, where legend says the devil buries treasure and Boulatruelle digs.
The woods round Montfermeil, where Thénardier catches up with the stranger and the child.
Village below Montfermeil toward the Marne.
Village on the Lagny road where the traveller leaves the coach after dark.
Village on the road below Montfermeil, where Boulatruelle mends the road.

places.name: Lagny
places.today: Lagny-sur-Marne.

tagline.text: Market town on the Marne, at the far end of Boulatruelle’s road.
Market town on the Marne, served by a coach from Paris.

places.name: Livry
places.today: Livry-Gargan.

tagline.text: Village north of Montfermeil.
Village north of Montfermeil, toward which the stranger and Cosette walk at daybreak.
Small walled town near the Channel coast, Fantine’s birthplace.
Fantine’s native town, made prosperous by Father Madeleine’s trade in black glass trinkets.
The town where Jean Valjean has lived as M. Madeleine, manufacturer and mayor.
The town whose prosperity collapses once its mayor is gone.
The great black-glass works, with separate workrooms for men and women, open to anyone honest.
The black-glass works, from whose women’s workroom Fantine is dismissed.
The mayor’s infirmary, kept by nursing sisters.
The mayor’s infirmary, where Fantine lies ill under Sister Simplice’s care.
The mayor’s infirmary, where Fantine dies.
Where Javert sentences Fantine to six months and the mayor sets her free.
Town five leagues from Montreuil, the first relay on the Arras road.
Town on the Arras road, where the tilbury’s wheel is found to be broken.

places.name: Saint-Pol
places.today: Saint-Pol-sur-Ternoise.

tagline.text: Town six leagues beyond Hesdin, the second relay on the road to Arras.
Cathedral city and seat of the département.
Cathedral city whose Assizes are trying a man arrested nearby as Jean Valjean.

places.name: The Assizes at Arras
places.today: The old bishop’s palace is now the Prefecture of the Pas-de-Calais.

tagline.text: The court of Assizes, sitting late in the old bishop’s palace, where Champmathieu is on trial.
The courtroom where Jean Valjean names himself before the jury.
Picard village near Amiens, Fauchelevent’s home country.
Capital of the Low Countries, behind Wellington’s lines; the great road runs to it across the battlefield.

places.name: Waterloo
places.today: The field lies in the communes of Braine-l’Alleud, Lasne and Waterloo; the village itself is four kilometres north.

tagline.text: Belgian battlefield where Napoleon’s last army was destroyed on 18 June 1815.
The battlefield south of the village of Waterloo, which the narrator walks in May 1861.
Belgian town from which the narrator walks north toward the battlefield.
Village whose church tower stands west of the road; one end of the hollow road of Ohain.

places.name: Hougomont
places.today: The farm still stands, restored in 2015.

tagline.text: Walled farm with a cannonball scar in its gate, the first sight of the battlefield.
Château-farm on the French left, where three thousand men died in one enclosure.
Village and farm on the plateau where Wellington held the high ground.
The plateau where the English squares stood for two hours under the cuirassiers.
Inn on the Genappe road at the foot of Hugo’s A, where Napoleon stood.
Farm and heights south of La Belle-Alliance, Napoleon’s first post on the morning of the battle.

places.name: The hollow road of Ohain
places.today: Mostly levelled when its banks were dug away to build the Lion Mound.

tagline.text: Sunken lane along the crest of Mont-Saint-Jean, the crossbar of Hugo’s A.
The sunken lane, invisible from below, into which Ney’s cuirassiers plunge until it is filled.
The sunken lane where, that night, a prowler named Thénardier robs an officer named Pontmercy, who thinks himself rescued.

places.name: The Lion Mound
places.today: The Butte du Lion, finished in 1826.

tagline.text: The monument raised on the centre of the battlefield, where the last word of the battle was spoken.
Farm on the Brussels road in front of the English centre, stormed and carried.
Farm on the Brussels road, taken by the French; only forty-two of its German defenders survive.
Farm on the English left, attacked by Ney and taken.
Village behind the French right.
Village behind the French right, where Bülow’s Prussians come out of the forest.
Heights on the far east of the field, the end of the line of English campfires.
Heights to the east, where bayonets gleam at five o’clock.
Town on the Dyle to the east, where the Prussians are delayed at the bridge.

places.name: The Abbey of Villers
places.today: Villers Abbey, Villers-la-Ville.

tagline.text: Ruined abbey near Brussels, whose in pace dungeons Hugo saw himself.

places.name: Saint-Sulpice
places.today: The church of Saint-Sulpice, 6th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Great church of the Left Bank, between the Luxembourg and Saint-Germain.

places.name: Les Halles

tagline.text: The central markets of Paris.

places.name: The Champ-de-Mars
places.today: The park beneath the Eiffel Tower, built in 1889.

tagline.text: Great parade-ground in front of the École Militaire.

places.name: Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas
places.today: The church still stands on the Rue Saint-Jacques, 5th arrondissement.

tagline.text: Parish church on the Rue Saint-Jacques, near the Val-de-Grâce.

places.name: The Luxembourg garden
places.today: The Jardin du Luxembourg, seat of the French Senate.

tagline.text: The great garden of the Left Bank, loved by students and lovers.

places.name: The Porte Saint-Martin
places.today: The arch still stands on the Boulevard Saint-Martin.

tagline.text: Triumphal arch on the Grands Boulevards, with a popular theatre beside it.

places.name: The police post in the Rue de Pontoise
places.today: The Rue de Pontoise, 5th arrondissement, near the Seine.

tagline.text: Street on the Left Bank with a commissary of police’s office.

places.name: The Faubourg Saint-Antoine
places.today: The Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Antoine, 11th and 12th arrondissements.

tagline.text: Working-class suburb east of the Bastille.

places.name: Père-Lachaise

tagline.text: The great cemetery on the eastern hills of Paris, burial-place of the well-to-do.
